items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 1:57AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding, large breaking waves
of 5 to 8 feet, and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...Through this evening for the High Surf Advisory and
through Monday for the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Rip
Current Risk.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 12:43AM EDT until November 2 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
An upper-level low will move atop Florida today through Monday. This
feature will add more moisture and support for showers and storms
than recent days. Strong low-level easterly flow will result in bands
of repeated rainfall for isolated to scattered locations. Showers and
storms are expected to be a bit more widespread with higher rain
rates than the past few days.

* WHAT...Bands of heavy rain may cause urban and street flooding.

* WHERE...All of Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties.

* WHEN...From 10 AM EST this morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered area of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Uncertainty is high regarding exactly where the highest rain
amounts will fall. However, scattered locations across the east
coast may pick up 3 to 5 inches of rain through Monday. Isolated
spots may see accumulations as high as 5 to 7 inches. These
amounts may fall over a window of a few hours. Expected impacts
could be greater than forecast if the heaviest rainfall occurs
near the coast during times of high tide.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 1 at 1:58AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas
5 to 8 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach
FL out 20 NM, Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean
Reef FL out 20 NM, Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield
Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM and Waters from Deerfield Beach to
Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial
waters of Bahamas.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
